label: prop:a2-from-three-strands
title: The $A_2$ root system from the Hecke algebra $H_3(q)$
html:
Proposition. The A_2 root system from the Hecke algebra H_3(q)

The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q) has Coxeter type A_2, and the associated weight lattice supplies the (I_3, Y) coordinates used throughout this chapter.

Scope. This is a statement about the A_2 of the Coxeter group W(A_2) \cong S_3 acting on the three strands, and it holds by construction: the braid group on n strands has Coxeter type A_{n-1}, so n = 3 puts A_2 here by definition. Nothing about the substrate is derived from it. In particular this is not the A_2 = \mathfrak{sl}_3 of flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}, which is the Schur--Weyl partner acting on the fibre V and requires \dim V = 3 (Proposition, where the framework supplies \dim V = 2). Items 1--3 below are the standard braid/Coxeter dictionary, recorded for reference; item 4 and the weight-lattice paragraph are what the chapter actually uses.

Concretely:

  1. The generators T_1, T_2 of H_3(q) satisfy the braid relation T_1 T_2 T_1 = T_2 T_1 T_2 and the quadratic Hecke relation (T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The braid relation is the defining relation of the Coxeter group W(A_2) \cong S_3.

  2. The Cartan matrix of A_2 is

  a_{ij}
  = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}.

This is read off from the Coxeter presentation in the usual way: the braid relation T_1 T_2 T_1 = T_2 T_1 T_2 has length m_{12} = 3, and a_{ij} = -2\cos(\pi/m_{ij}) gives a_{12} = a_{21} = -1, with a_{ii} = 2 by normalisation. For |i - j| > 1 the generators commute (m_{ij} = 2) and a_{ij} = 0. Earlier drafts wrote this as a counting formula a_{ij} = 2\delta_{ij} - |\{T_iT_jT_i = T_jT_iT_j\}|; that formula is a re-encoding of the presentation, not an independent derivation of the Cartan data, and is withdrawn to avoid suggesting otherwise.

  1. The six roots of A_2 are the elements \{\pm\alpha_1, \pm\alpha_2, \pm(\alpha_1 + \alpha_2)\}, where \alpha_1, \alpha_2 are the simple roots associated to T_1, T_2. The angle between adjacent roots is \pi/3 (that is, 120° between a root and its negative), reflecting the Coxeter number h = 3 of A_2. The Weyl group W(A_2) \cong S_3 acts by permuting the three strands.

  2. At q = 1 (the classical limit), H_3(q) reduces to the group algebra \mathbb{C}[S_3], and the A_2 root system is the standard one. For q \neq 1 (the substrate-deformed case), the root system acquires a q-deformed inner product: the quantum Killing form \langle \alpha_i, \alpha_j \rangle_q = [a_{ij}]_q, where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer.

The hexagonal weight lattice of A_2 is the 2-dimensional lattice generated by the fundamental weights \omega_1, \omega_2 dual to the simple roots. Each irreducible representation of H_3(q) is labelled by a dominant integral weight (\lambda_1, \lambda_2) with \lambda_i \geq 0, and the weights of the representation sit at the vertices of a hexagonal pattern in the (I_3, Y) plane, where

  I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2),
  \qquad
  Y   = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2).

The fundamental representation \mathbf{3} has weights \{(1,0), (0,1), (-1,-1)\}, forming an equilateral triangle. The adjoint representation \mathbf{8} has weights forming a regular hexagon with multiplicity 2 at the origin.
